messages:
Arjun: heads-up — nightly smoke shows a regression on MoE runs when we scale > 4 nodes. tail latency spikes ~2x; root appears to be an all-to-all hotspot during routing. cc @Maria @Jess

Maria: can you paste the perf slice you captured? was this during 1k seq or longer sequences?

Arjun: repro config: 8xA100, TP=1, PP=1, TP shards not changing. seq=1536, batch=32 (dynamic batching enabled). here's the flame slice around routing: 
```
[trace] stage: routing.expert_all2all_nccl  duration=42.1ms  (expected ~10-12ms)
[trace] stage: kv_cache_write        duration=8.3ms
[trace] stage: expert_compute        duration=11.6ms
[trace] stage: allreduce_grad        duration=4.2ms
```
Looks like nccl all-to-all is dominant.

Jess: interesting — kernel_selector jumped to the safe kernel path for the expert matmuls when seq>1024, that could increase compute but not 4x. do you have per-expert assignment skew?

Sam: ran a quick router heatmap (hotspot counts per expert) — 2 experts are getting ~4-5x the tokens. probably uneven gating output for these prompts. heatmap: `[[0,1,0,0,5,4,0,...]]` (pseudo).

Ryan: hypothesis: (1) skewed expert traffic causing buffer/memory pressure -> extra memcpy/alltoall ops, (2) KV cache behavior on warm-starts produces additional fanout (we write new keys then broadcast), (3) NCCL fallback/algorithm choice is poor for this message size.

perf-bot: artifacts uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood/1976543210/moe-alltoall/trace.html — includes per-rank timeline and nccl algorithm selection logs.

Arjun: I inspected the nccl logs from artifact. NCCL selected `TREE` for alltoall with nbytes=~1.8MB which is poor on our topology. switching to `RING` reduced single-call latency in microbench by ~30%. snippet: 
```
NCCL_ALGO=RING python tools/microbench_alltoall.py --size 1835008 --ranks 8
# before: 12.4ms  after: 8.6ms
```

Maria: good find. also we should consider overlapping: we currently run all2all then compute; runtime can overlap if we async-launch kernel for expert compute while all2all streams run. check `--overlap-all2all` flag in runtime.

Jess: kernel selection note — when quantized kernels are enabled we see different scheduling: the runtime picks `q_mlp_launcher` which uses a different launch config that hurts co-operative overlap. need to verify kernel launch streams.

Sam: quick repro plan: 1) replay problematic prompt set with `--trace=timeline`, 2) force NCCL_ALGO=RING, 3) run with `--enable-routing-shuffle-buffering` disabled to see KV write effect, 4) toggle `--overlap-all2all` to measure overlap gain. I'll kick it off on `eng-runtime/ci-large` now.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy `moe-routing-fix-try` triggered on pool `ci-large` (job id 83921).

perf-bot: initial canary results uploaded: 1976543210/canary-83921/summary.json — ring algo reduces all2all P50 by ~35% but P99 still high.

Ryan: if P99 is still high maybe the root cause is queueing on a single GPU waiting for its turn to alltoall (hotspot expert). need to instrument per-rank enqueue waits. also try alternative routing: top-2 -> randomized tie-breaker to reduce concentrated load.

Maria: agreed. small change that randomizes tie-break in router might reduce hotspot without hurting quality. we should A/B with eval set. I can prepare the eval harness for quality regression.

Arjun: action items: Sam -> reproduce with the 4 toggles (nccl/ring, overlap on/off, buffering on/off, tie-break randomized) and attach timeline + per-rank waits. Jess -> check kernel streams + quantized launch path for overlap regressions. Maria -> run quality A/B for randomized tie-break. Ryan -> look into NCCL tuning knobs and ops-level socket topology mapping. I'll coordinate and sync results tomorrow.

Sam: started run, will post logs when done (job 83921).

Arjun: thanks — if anyone sees quick wins (e.g., force ring + overlap) and can patch a canary, do it. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Note: staging NCCL updated to 2.12 last week; prod still on 2.10. Upgrading prod will require a rolling restart of dedicated clusters. filing infra ticket INF-1142.

Jess: FYI — found a micro-issue: when `--enable-prefix-cache` is true and batch has many short sequences, router issues an alltoall per-example instead of batching them due to cache miss logic. that explodes small alltoall counts. patch incoming.

Arjun: perfect — that patch + ring + overlap sounds promising. let's reconvene after Sam posts canary timelines.

perf-bot: job 83921 logs: https://artifacts.redwood/1976543210/canary-83921/logs.txt

Sam: canary done: ring + overlap + cache-fix reduced P99 by ~28% on the prompt set. attaching timeline in artifact.

Arjun: great, prioritizing a staged rollback and follow-up perf patch. thanks everyone.
